title: Restricted Parallel V1 Wall-Clock Scaling & Worker-Cost Characterization
purpose: Characterize wall-clock scaling and incremental worker cost of the already-qualified F-MR20 parallel-v1 path without changing physics, admission, solver policy, mass tolerances or production source.
hard_source_rule: No file under src/ may differ from the exact F-MR20 closeout base for F-PE07 measurement or closeout.

frozen_physical_profile.state_handle_contract: one unique committed-state handle per logical column

timing_arms.name: W1
timing_arms.route: fmr_run_parallel_physical_multiswap single-worker delegation to serialized reference

timing_design.measurement_clock: Fortran system_clock around only the runtime dispatch call
included_in_timed_region: backend initialization performed by the runtime
batch barriers and OpenMP team management for W2/W4

aggregation.primary: median per-arm wall time and derived median speedup W1/W2 and W1/W4
aggregation.tail: p95 per-arm wall time and p95 paired block-normalized ratios

pre_timing_hard_gates: no src/ changes relative to F-MR20 closeout
existing F-MR20 parallel-v1 scientific qualification remains green
all timed arms commit all 32 columns on every measured dispatch
W2 shows at least two simultaneous real physical solves
W4 shows at least two simultaneous real physical solves
scientific state/result identity is not weakened for timing
reported_metrics: incremental wall-clock overhead or benefit relative to W1
observed simultaneous real physical solve count
interpretation_limits: GitHub-hosted runner timings are environment-specific characterization, not universal hardware guarantees
F-PE07 does not qualify other column counts or batch sizes
F-PE07 does not widen the frozen F-MR20 physical profile
F-PE07 does not alter solver tolerances, physics or mass policy to obtain speedup
a speedup below 1 is valid negative evidence and must be persisted
timing results do not by themselves prove large-scale MultiSWAP scaling
